title: test-0103-SOC-ECO-SECTORS
passage: The Indian economy is divided into three sectors based on the nature of activities. The primary sector involves extracting natural resources, which includes not just farming, but also fishing, mining, and forestry. When these raw materials are transformed into finished products, we enter the secondary sector. The tertiary sector provides essential services that support the other two. To measure the total economic health of the nation, we calculate the Gross Domestic Product (GDP). GDP is defined as the total value of all final goods and services produced within a country during a particular year. It is not merely the count of physical goods, but the monetary value of everything produced. Furthermore, the government plays a vital role through the public sector, which provides essential services like healthcare and education to ensure social welfare, regardless of whether these services generate immediate financial profit. To support rural livelihoods, the government also implements schemes like MGNREGA. This act guarantees one hundred days of wage employment in a year for rural households, specifically targeting those in need of work in villages, rather than providing jobs to urban residents. By understanding these distinctions, we can better analyze how different sectors contribute to our national development and employment stability.
